claim: US police do not only buy Israeli hardware — American law-enforcement officials travel to Israel for training. The Anti-Defamation League (ADL), by its own account, ran a Leadership Seminar that "from 1987-2019 ... brought small groups of senior American law enforcement leaders to Israel for a week-long seminar," and has run a separate National Counter-Terrorism Seminar since 2004 that more than 200 law-enforcement executives from over 100 US and foreign departments have attended. The Jewish Institute for National Security of America (JINSA) and Georgia State University's GILEE (Georgia International Law Enforcement Exchange) run parallel delegations. A 2018 report by Jewish Voice for Peace and the Research and Advocacy Initiative, titled "Deadly Exchange," argued these trips transfer surveillance, racial-profiling, and crowd-control tactics used in the occupied territories to US policing. The ADL rejects that characterization and, after the campaign, revised its curriculum but chose to keep the program running.

sources.label: Anti-Defamation League — "Responding to Questions about ADL's Law Enforcement Leadership Seminars in Israel." ADL's own description of the program and its run dates.
